rose-plugs.tagline: A home of Rosie's own in Settings, with one-tap installs for anything not installed yet.
rose-plugs.howItWorks: Adds a "Rosie's Plugs" section to Discord's Settings, separate from Revenge's own Plugins list. Its first entry, "Plugins," is a quick-install browser pulling live from this site's own plugin catalog, grouped by category, with a one-tap button per row that installs or removes it directly. Every other Rosie-authored plugin that's currently installed gets a direct settings shortcut listed right below it, and RosePlugs' own settings live in that same section too.
features: New top-level "Rosie's Plugs" settings section, positioned right below Revenge's own
One-tap install/uninstall browser for every plugin in this catalog, grouped by category
Direct settings shortcuts for each installed Rosie-authored plugin - no digging through Revenge's own Plugins list
rose-plugs.limitations: Only surfaces plugins whose manifest lists "Rosie" as an author - a plugin credited to someone else (like Raiden's Themes, credited to the original theme's creator) won't be picked up automatically.

radial-status.tagline: A colored ring around the avatar instead of a presence dot - similar to Platform Indicator, but for status.
radial-status.note: Fork of AngelW0lf's Radial Status (BSD-3-Clause, see LICENSE). Upstream had a phone-home mechanism - it fetched a remote blacklist on every load and could silently uninstall itself for specific user IDs the original author chose - dropped entirely here, no network requests at all. Upstream only ever matched one exact avatar size (member list-style rows), missing YouBar, the profile screen, and DM lists entirely. On-device capture across all of those contexts confirmed the real presence-carrying wrapper sizes (24, 32, 40, 50, 60, 80px) all share the same shape - square, half-width border radius, exactly 5 children - so this fork matches that confirmed whitelist instead of either upstream's single size or an earlier overly-broad generalization that briefly caused visible corruption elsewhere on-device. Also switched the ring's size growth from a percentage multiplier to a fixed pixel amount: a flat multiplier applied the same 30% growth everywhere, which meant a much bigger absolute size increase on large avatars (confirmed on-device as noticeably oversized on YouBar) than on small ones - fixed-px growth keeps the ring the same absolute thickness regardless of avatar size. Upstream's settings screen had commented-out, non-functional size/thickness inputs and an unfinished joke placeholder button - both removed, with a real working thickness control in their place.
radial-status.howItWorks: Hides the small colored dot Discord shows on an avatar for online/idle/DND/offline, and draws a colored ring around the whole avatar instead - similar in spirit to a platform indicator, but for presence status. Each status's color is independently configurable (including offline, which Discord doesn't normally show a dot for at all), along with the ring's thickness. A status left with no color configured just keeps showing the normal dot.
features: Colored ring around the avatar instead of the small presence dot
Independent color per status: online, idle, do not disturb, offline
Adjustable ring thickness, sized consistently across every avatar context
No network requests - upstream's remote blacklist/kill-switch mechanism was removed entirely
radial-status.limitations: Matches a whitelist of avatar sizes confirmed on-device across YouBar, the profile screen, member lists, and DM lists - not a fully generic circular-wrapper match, since an earlier attempt at that briefly caused visible corruption on unrelated UI elements. A future Discord update introducing a new avatar size in one of these contexts (or elsewhere) wouldn't be picked up until re-confirmed and added to the whitelist.

custom-user-tags.tagline: Create your own tags and assign them to specific users - not tied to server permissions.
custom-user-tags.note: Didn't exist in the Revenge/Vendetta plugin ecosystem before. Modeled directly on Staff Tags' proven 4-surface architecture (the chat message tag, the name row in chat/member list/profile, and the native Tag component itself), keyed by user ID instead of permission tier - the same code, resolving a completely different kind of tag.
custom-user-tags.howItWorks: Long-press a name in the member list or a profile popout to open a small editor: type whatever text you want and pick a color, and that becomes their tag - showing next to their name in chat, the member list, and the profile popout, exactly like a Staff Tags tag would. There's no confirmed way in this repo yet to hook Discord's own native long-press menu for a user, so this attaches its own long-press handler directly to the row instead (chaining whatever Discord's own row already does, never replacing it). Tags can also be added from the plugin's own settings screen by pasting a user ID directly, for tagging someone who isn't visible on screen right now.
features: Long-press a member list row or profile popout to tag someone
Custom tag text and a full color picker, not limited to preset tiers
Also shows in chat messages next to the author's name
Add/remove tags by user ID from the settings screen
Per-user, not per-permission - works for anyone regardless of their server roles
custom-user-tags.limitations: Chat message tags are built from plain data passed to Discord's native row renderer, not a patchable React element, so they always render as a solid color there - same platform limitation Staff Tags documents. Long-press to open the editor is a plugin-attached handler, not a native Discord menu item, since no confirmed way to add one exists yet.

staff-tags.tagline: OWNER/ADMIN/STAFF/MOD tags, computed from real permissions - not role names.
staff-tags.note: Previously broken. Rebuilt with per-patch crash isolation, plus new customization: per-tag text, colors, gradients, and visibility.
staff-tags.howItWorks:
Staff Tags looks at what a member can actually do in a server - Administrator, Manage Server, Manage Messages, Kick/Ban, and so on - and shows a small colored tag next to their name based on the highest-matching tier. It doesn't care what a role is named, so a role called "Cool Person" with Manage Messages still shows MOD. Tags appear in chat messages, the member list, the profile popout, and channel headers.

The old version of this plugin patched four separate Discord UI surfaces, and if Discord renamed even one internal component, the whole plugin's setup would throw and every tag everywhere would silently disappear. This rebuild wraps each of the four patches in its own guard, so a single broken surface degrades gracefully instead of taking the other three down with it.
features: Seven built-in tiers: Webhook, Owner, Admin, Staff, Mod, VC Mod, Chat Mod
Per-tag show/hide toggle
Custom tag text (rename "MOD" to whatever you want)
Custom solid colors with a swatch picker
Gradient tags in the member list and profile (chat tags stay solid - platform limitation, explained below)
"Use top role color" fallback when no custom color is set
staff-tags.limitations: Gradient colors only render in the member list and profile popout. Chat message tags are built from plain data passed to Discord's native row renderer, not a patchable React element, so there's no element to swap in a gradient view - they always fall back to a solid color there.

role-color-everywhere.tagline: A member's role color, applied everywhere Discord doesn't already show it.
role-color-everywhere.note: Previously broken. Ported from the original source and hardened with the same crash-isolation fix as Staff Tags.
role-color-everywhere.howItWorks: Discord already colors a message author's name by their top role - this extends that same color into places Discord leaves plain: @mentions inside message text, the "X is typing..." indicator, voice channel participant lists, and the role section headers in the member list. There's also an optional (off by default) mode that tints the message text itself toward the author's color, though that comes with a real tradeoff: it disables text selection on tinted messages, since the coloring works by wrapping the text in a link-style element.
features: Colored @mentions in chat
Colored typing indicator
Colored voice channel participant names
Colored member list role section headers
Optional message-text tinting with an adjustable strength slider (0-100)
Every surface can be toggled independently
role-color-everywhere.limitations: The member list header coloring works by patching a generic, unnamed internal component (there's no dedicated "RoleHeader" component to target), which makes it the single most fragile surface in this plugin. If a future Discord update breaks it, the other four surfaces are unaffected.

pronoun-db.tagline: Shows a user's pronouns in their profile, pulled from pronoundb.org.
pronoun-db.note: Previously broken because PronounDB shut down the API it used (HTTP 410) - migrated to their current v2 API. Also fixed the profile-page lookup itself: Discord renamed the top-level profile component to UserProfileContent and the bio card to UserProfileAboutMeCard (confirmed against decompiled current-build source), so both the new and old names are checked. Requires people to have set pronouns at pronoundb.org; nothing to configure in the plugin itself.
pronoun-db.howItWorks: PronounDB is a separate, independent service (not run by Discord or Revenge) where people manually set their own pronouns once and link the profile to their Discord account. This plugin adds a "Pronouns" section near the bio on anyone's profile who has done that. Lookups are batched and cached client-side, so opening a profile for the first time may take a moment while it fetches, and re-opening the same profile later is instant.
features: Adds a native-feeling "Pronouns" section to profiles
Batches and caches lookups so scrolling through many profiles doesn't spam requests
Nothing to configure - no API key, no toggle
pronoun-db.limitations: Only shows pronouns for people who have actually created a PronounDB profile and linked their Discord account. If nobody you interact with has set one, you'll never see the section - that's expected, not a bug.

message-snippets.tagline: Save reusable text once, send it anywhere with a slash command.
message-snippets.note: Didn't exist in the Revenge/Vendetta plugin ecosystem before.
message-snippets.howItWorks: Save a name and a block of text once - server rules, an FAQ answer, your PayPal, whatever you type often - then send it in any server or DM with a single command instead of retyping or copy-pasting from notes. Snippets are stored locally on your device and sync with nothing external. Built entirely on Revenge's built-in command API rather than patching Discord's UI internals, so it doesn't carry the "might silently break on a Discord update" risk that UI-patching plugins do.
features: /snippet <name> sends the saved text as a real message
Manage everything from the plugin's settings screen: add, preview, and delete
Slash-command management too: /snippet-save, /snippet-delete, /snippet-list
No character limit beyond Discord's own message limit

commands.desc: Sends the saved snippet as a message in the current channel
Shows your saved snippet names as a toast (not posted publicly)

reminders.tagline: Quick reminders without leaving the chat you're in.
reminders.note: Didn't exist in the Revenge/Vendetta plugin ecosystem before. Only fires while Discord is running.
reminders.howItWorks: Set a reminder with a simple duration and a note, and it'll pop up as an in-app alert once it's due - no need to switch apps or set a system alarm. Reminders are checked every 15 seconds while the plugin is loaded and persist in local storage, so they survive a plugin reload, but not a fully closed app: pure-JS plugins can't schedule native OS notifications, so this can only fire while Discord's process is actually alive (foreground or backgrounded-but-running).
features: Flexible duration parsing: 10m, 2h, 1d, 30sec, 1 week, and more
See and cancel pending reminders from the plugin's settings screen
Persists across a plugin reload

commands.desc: e.g. /remind 20m Walk the dog - fires an in-app alert when it's due

reminders.limitations: Can't wake Discord up from fully closed - that needs a native OS-level scheduled notification, which isn't something a JS-only plugin has access to. If you force-close the app, pending reminders resume checking once you reopen it, but won't have fired while it was closed.

view-raw.tagline: See a message's raw JSON - searchable, syntax-highlighted, and copyable.
view-raw.note: Fork of bwlok's ViewRaw (GPLv3 - see the plugin's own LICENSE file). Fixed a crash that hit every message long-press, then rebuilt the viewer with search and syntax highlighting on top.
view-raw.howItWorks: Long-press any message and pick "View Raw" to see exactly what Discord sent for it - every field, not just the rendered text. The original plugin crashed the long-press menu on every message because it assumed a specific internal icon shape without checking it first; this fork guards that assumption and everything else in the same patch. The viewer itself was rebuilt: a search box highlights matching lines (dimming the rest, not hiding them, so you keep the structure for context), values are color-coded by type, and there are one-tap copy buttons for either just the message content or the full JSON.
features: Search box highlights matching keys/values across the whole payload
Syntax-colored JSON (strings, numbers, booleans, null all render differently)
Separate "Copy Content" and "Copy JSON" buttons
Crash fixed: no longer breaks the message long-press menu
view-raw.limitations: Licensed GPLv3 (inherited from the original), not the same terms as the rest of this repo - see plugins/view-raw/LICENSE. The long-press button relies on detecting Discord's internal action-sheet layout (not an official API) - the plugin's settings screen shows diagnostics if it ever stops appearing.

key-inspector.tagline: One-tap diagnostic scan of every internal key this repo's plugins depend on - copy the report, no computer needed.
key-inspector.note: Built to support fixing other broken plugins in this ecosystem entirely from a phone: most crashes come from a plugin assuming an internal key/component still exists after a Discord update, and this lets anyone check on-device and share the exact result.
key-inspector.howItWorks: The main feature is a full scan: one button runs every internal lookup (findByProps, findByName, findByStoreName, specific semanticColors tokens) that this repo's plugins actually depend on, all in one pass, and copies a complete found/missing report plus the full current semanticColors and rawColors key lists to your clipboard. There's also a manual search section for anything not already in the scan list - type prop names or a component name and copy what findByProps/findByName returns for it. Nothing leaves your device; everything only touches your clipboard.
features: Full scan: every known lookup, checked in one tap, with a copyable report
Full Vendetta API tree: every key path Revenge exposes to plugins, 3 levels deep, in one copy
Manual findByProps(...) / findByName(...) search for anything else
Includes the complete semanticColors and rawColors key lists
No network requests, no data collection - clipboard only
key-inspector.limitations: The full-scan list only covers lookups this repo's plugins currently use - it's meant to grow as more plugins get added or fixed. The API tree covers Revenge's own plugin API (window.vendetta), not Discord's raw internal module registry, which is far too large to dump wholesale - use the search tools for that.

better-timestamps.tagline: Calendar-relative, fully relative, ISO 8601, or your own custom timestamp format.
better-timestamps.note: Previously broken (unguarded RowManager lookup). Rebuilt with the same crash-isolation pattern as the rest of this repo.
better-timestamps.howItWorks: Replaces both message timestamps and the "day divider" text in chat with your choice of format: calendar-relative ("Yesterday at 3:04 PM"), fully relative ("2 hours ago"), ISO 8601, or a fully custom moment.js format string. There's also a toggle to always show the name/avatar/timestamp on every message instead of Discord's default grouping of consecutive messages.
features: Four built-in formats plus a custom moment.js format string
Live preview of each format in the settings screen
Applies to both message timestamps and day dividers
Optional: always show name/avatar/timestamp per message

copy-role-color.tagline: Long-press a role pill to copy its color as hex.
copy-role-color.note: Previously broken - the component was renamed from ThemedRolePill to just RolePill (confirmed against decompiled current-build Discord source), so the old lookup never found anything. Now checks both names, with defensive checks throughout so a shape mismatch never crashes.
copy-role-color.howItWorks: Long-press a role pill - in the member list, a role list, wherever Discord renders one as its own element - and the color gets copied to your clipboard as a hex code. Useful for designers, bot builders, or staff matching embed colors to a role.
features: Works on any rendered role pill, not just one specific screen
Copies a ready-to-paste hex code (e.g. #5865F2)
copy-role-color.limitations: Depends on Discord's internal role pill component keeping a similar shape - guarded so a mismatch just means no long-press handler gets added, not a crash.

urban-dictionary.tagline: Look up a definition without leaving Discord.
urban-dictionary.note: Previously broken (dead proxy host). Rebuilt from scratch on the stable command API - no UI patching involved.
urban-dictionary.howItWorks: Runs your term against Urban Dictionary's public API and posts the top result - definition, example, and the up/downvote count - directly into the channel. Built entirely on the same stable command API as Message Snippets and Reminders, so it doesn't carry the UI-patching fragility that most of this repo's revived plugins have to guard against.
features: Posts the definition, an example, and vote counts
Truncates long entries so they stay readable in chat

commands.desc: Looks up a term and posts the top Urban Dictionary result

urban-dictionary.limitations: Urban Dictionary's community submissions are what they are - results aren't moderated by this plugin.

reverse-image-search.tagline: Open an image link in Google Lens, Yandex, or TinEye.
reverse-image-search.note: Didn't exist in the Revenge/Vendetta plugin ecosystem before.
reverse-image-search.howItWorks: Long-press an image in Discord, choose "Copy Media Link", then run this command with that link to open it in a reverse image search engine of your choice. Built purely on opening a URL - no Discord-internal patching at all, so it's about as low-risk as a plugin gets.
features: Supports Google Lens, Yandex, and TinEye
Defaults to Google Lens if no engine is specified

commands.desc: Opens the image in your browser's reverse image search

reverse-image-search.limitations: Needs a direct image URL, not a Discord attachment reference - use "Copy Media Link" first.

fake-profile-themes-and-effects.tagline: Profile theming and profile effects without Nitro.
fake-profile-themes-and-effects.note: Fork of shipwr3ckd's FPTE. Previously crashed every time you opened the profile editor - confirmed via on-device diagnostics that several color tokens it referenced (HEADER_SECONDARY, BACKGROUND_PRIMARY, BACKGROUND_FLOATING, TEXT_NORMAL) no longer exist on current Discord builds. Rebuilt with a fallback chain of real, currently-valid token names instead of a single hardcoded one. A second, separate bug (an unguarded lookup that crashed the whole plugin bundle before it could even load) is also fixed.
fake-profile-themes-and-effects.howItWorks: Encodes your chosen primary color, accent color, and profile effect into invisible zero-width characters appended to your About Me - other people running a compatible plugin (this one, or the original) decode and render it as if you had real Nitro profile theming, without Discord's servers ever knowing. The builder UI for picking colors/effects lives right in the profile editor. Only the two files that were actually confirmed crashing were investigated and fixed; the rest of this plugin's original patches (Nitro upsell card, purchase checks, profile data fetching) are carried over as-is, now with crash isolation so any other latent issue only disables that one patch instead of the whole plugin.
features: Pick a primary color, accent color, and profile effect from the profile editor
No Nitro required - works purely by encoding data into your bio
Crash isolation per patch, so one broken surface doesn't take down the rest
fake-profile-themes-and-effects.limitations: Only the confirmed profile-editor crash was root-caused and fixed with real on-device data. The plugin's other patches (Nitro upsell card, purchase/profile data fetching) weren't individually re-audited - crash isolation means a problem there disables just that patch rather than the whole plugin, but hasn't been proven bug-free the way the color-resolution fix has.

rose-utils.tagline: Spotify listen-along, colorful channels, a full Message Logger, and more - independently toggleable modules.
rose-utils.note: Fork of nexpid's NexxUtils. Originally revived by fixing a class-vs-function-component crash in Spotify listen-along and a build bug that silently dropped every module's own error/patch tracking. Since then: Developer Mode was expanded into a general dev-tools module (message and server info copy-ID tools too), the Tenor GIF fix was dropped (no longer needed), and the settings screen gained search, mass enable/disable, and collapsible categories as the module count grew. Newest addition: Message Logger, a full deleted/edited message logger with a searchable on-device viewer, persisted across restarts.
rose-utils.howItWorks: Each utility is its own independently toggleable module, with its own settings shown once enabled: Spotify listen-along buttons on activities, a Spotify listen-along invite button in the attachment menu, a "minimod" showing member timeouts in chat, colorful/NSFW-tagged channel icons, an expanded Developer Mode (keeps Discord's own toggle on, adds copy-ID rows for slash-command interactions and activity/game IDs), extra message long-press copy-ID tools (webhook ID, nonce, attachment IDs, replied-to message ID, debug info), server info/friends-in-server tools, a snowflake ID timestamp decoder, and Message Logger. The settings screen has a search box, per-category collapse, and bulk enable/disable, since the module count has grown past what a flat list handles well. Every module tracks its own errors and shows a one-tap "copy report" row if something goes wrong.
features: Spotify listen-along buttons on activities, plus an invite button in the attachment menu
Message Logger: deleted/edited message log, persisted on-device, searchable viewer, ignore lists, keyword filters, per-channel/total/age limits
Minimod: shows member timeouts in chat
Colorful, NSFW-tagged channel icons
Expanded Developer Mode with extra copy-ID tools (commands, activities, webhooks, nonces, attachments, replies, server info)
Snowflake ID timestamp decoder
Per-module error tracking with one-tap copy for bug reports
Settings screen: search, collapsible categories, bulk enable/disable
rose-utils.limitations: The original's Material-Design component reskin isn't included (needs react-native-reanimated, not part of this build). Message Logger can only log messages Discord's own client has actually cached locally - it can't recover a deleted message it never saw, and attachment files themselves aren't re-hosted after Discord's CDN removes them (only the URL/filename/metadata are kept).

server-drawer.tagline: An expandable server grid with DMs, smarter folders, and mark-all-read built in.
server-drawer.note: Fork of kmmiio99o's ServerDrawer. One lookup (useMobileQuestDock) was missing an optional-chaining guard - if that lookup came back empty, the whole onLoad threw and every patch after it in the sequence never got applied, not just that one surface. Fixed, plus every patch call is now wrapped so a single bad lookup only skips its own surface. Folder options (auto-collapse, hide preview icons) are adapted from fres621's BetterFolders - its icon-hiding half patched a "GuildContainer" component that no longer exists anywhere in current Discord builds (confirmed against decompiled source), and only applied to the native server rail anyway, which this plugin already replaces - so it's been rebuilt as a feature of the drawer's own folders instead. Two more bugs fixed after real device testing: guild icons that never loaded (GuildStore lookups weren't reactive to guild data streaming in after connect, so most servers just showed a bare unread dot with no icon) and taps in the drawer not navigating anywhere (several lookups - transitionToGuild, the create/join action, the root nav ref - were resolved once at plugin-load time, before Discord had necessarily required those modules yet, same class of bug as YouBar+'s startup race). Both fixed; DMs also moved from a leftover sidebar icon into the drawer itself, and a mark-all-servers-as-read button was added. Two more rounds after that: the Quest Dock hijack (10 separate internal lookups just to force it to render) used to be attempted once at onLoad, so if any single one of them wasn't registered in Metro yet the drawer could just silently not show up for the whole session - it now retries whatever hasn't landed on a fast 200ms interval until everything's applied. And mark-all-read was rebuilt to match Discord's own markGuildsAsRead action exactly (getSelectableChannelIds + getVocalChannelIds per guild, confirmed against decompiled source) instead of a less certain guild-enumeration method. The left server rail hiding was also fixed properly this round: the rail's root component has no discoverable name at runtime at all (confirmed against decompiled source - it's a bare default export, and unlike memo-wrapped components with an explicit displayName, a plain function's own .name doesn't survive production minification), so every name-based lookup for it was guaranteed to fail. Now intercepted by its outermost View's literal nativeID ("guilds-bar-view", confirmed unique in the bundle) instead. The long-press context menu on a server icon had the exact same problem (getGuildsBarGuildMenuItems is also a bare default export) - replaced with a small menu of actions built from APIs this repo has already confirmed work (mark this server as read, copy server ID) instead of a lookup that could never succeed. The same caching bug affected several of ServerDrawer's own retry-based lookups (the Quest Dock hijack's fast-retry loop, and every findByProps call wrapped in the lazy() helper for navigation/action lookups) - all switched to a raw, uncached module scan for the specific calls that get retried, since a retried cached lookup was silently a no-op after its first failure.
server-drawer.howItWorks: Hijacks the Quest Dock - the strip Discord normally uses for daily quests, right above the tab bar - and puts a grid of your servers there instead. Tap it to expand, tap a server to jump to it, long-press for the usual context menu (mark as read, notification settings, leave, etc). A + button opens Discord's own create/join-server modal. Optionally hides the left server rail down to a single DMs icon, since your servers now live in the drawer instead.
features: Tap-to-expand server grid with folders, unread badges, and mention counts
Long-press a server for its real context menu, not a rebuilt one
One-tap create/join through Discord's native modal
Optional: collapse the left server rail to a single DMs icon
Toggle unread badges independently
Auto-collapse other open folders when you open a new one
Optional plain folder icon instead of the 4-server preview when collapsed
DMs tile in the drawer instead of a separate sidebar icon
Mark every channel in every server as read in one tap
server-drawer.limitations: Depends on several internal Quest Dock lookups (11 in total) - each is individually guarded, so a future Discord rename degrades one surface at a time instead of breaking the whole plugin. Drawer position (left/right/top) is still planned but not in this build yet - it currently only replaces the Quest Dock's native bottom position.

you-bar-plus.tagline: Adds DM and/or Settings buttons to the YouBar.
you-bar-plus.note: Fork of Purple-EyeZ's YouBar+. Fixed a startup race condition where the button patch could silently never apply for an entire session - the original did a single one-shot lookup for YouBarNotificationsButton at onLoad and gave up permanently if it wasn't registered in Metro yet, which restarting Discord only fixed by luck. Now retries until the component shows up. A second, deeper bug surfaced after that fix shipped: Revenge's own module finder permanently caches a "not found" result per search and never rescans, even after the target registers later - confirmed by reading Revenge's own source. That made the retry loop a no-op whenever the very first attempt happened too early, which is exactly the scenario it existed to handle. Now uses a raw, uncached module scan specifically for the retried lookup.
you-bar-plus.howItWorks: The YouBar is the row near your avatar/status at the top of the app. This plugin patches its notification button area to also render a DM button and/or a Settings button, each independently toggleable. DM jumps straight to your DMs; Settings opens user settings.
features: Independent toggles for the DM and Settings buttons
Settings changes apply immediately, no restart needed
Startup race condition fixed - polls for the target component instead of a single one-shot lookup
you-bar-plus.limitations: Depends on YouBarNotificationsButton keeping a similar render shape - guarded so a mismatch just means no extra buttons, not a crash.
